around.headline: Eight men get life imprisonment for killing youth in Bengaluru smoking-row
around.summary: A Bengaluru court sentenced eight men to life imprisonment for killing a youth after an argument that started over smoking, per today's report. It's a stark reminder to walk away from public disputes however trivial they start — de-escalation beats confrontation every time.

around.headline: Two killed in separate Bengaluru road accidents today
around.summary: Two people died in unrelated road accidents in the city today, per Deccan Herald. With a 90% rain chance tonight, slow down further at intersections and give extra following distance while riding or driving.

around.headline: Auto-taxi unions escalate protest against bike-taxi apps; bandh threat looms
around.summary: Private transport operators have moved from a 15-day deadline to an actual black-flag protest against bike-taxi aggregators, and are still threatening a citywide bandh if their demands aren't met, per today's reports. If you depend on autos or cabs, keep a backup transport plan ready over the next two weeks.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald, The Hindu

around.headline: 40 water tanker drivers booked for alleged drunk driving
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police booked 40 water tanker drivers on drunk-driving charges in a targeted crackdown, per Deccan Herald. Tankers are a known road hazard on residential streets — give them extra space, especially after dark.

around.headline: BESCOM's Gruha Jyothi verification drive finds many gates locked
around.summary: BESCOM's ongoing door-to-door verification for the free-electricity Gruha Jyothi scheme is running into locked gates across the city, per today's report, and a missed visit risks a lapse in the subsidy. If you're on the scheme and weren't home, call BESCOM (1912) to reschedule rather than wait for a second knock.

around.headline: Nepal flood death toll passes 600; over 300 Indians still unreachable
around.summary: Nepal's flash-flood death toll has crossed 600 as fresh glacial lakes form at the avalanche source, with more than 320 Indians still out of contact and roughly 400 stranded, per today's reports. If you have family or friends travelling in Nepal, keep checking in and watch for Karnataka government helpline updates.

street_smart.title: A man in a laminated ID badge knocks on your door saying he's from BESCOM, doing today's citywide Gruha Jyothi free-electricity verification round — like the drive making news today after finding many gates locked. He asks to see your Aadhaar card and a meter photo, then says he needs to confirm your registered mobile OTP to 'lock in' the scheme in the system before he moves to the next house. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real Bengaluru news: BESCOM's ongoing Gruha Jyothi (free electricity scheme) verification drive found many households' gates locked during today's citywide sweep, per The Times of India — meaning genuine BESCOM staff really are going door-to-door right now. That creates a fresh opening for doorstep impersonation scams. No utility- or scheme-impersonation-at-your-door scenario has been used as street-smart in the last three weeks — recent scams covered bank-OTP phone calls (this morning), digital arrest, and Cognizant vishing, all phone-based rather than an in-person doorstep con; every evergreen rotation topic has also already run within the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: A minute later, he adds that if you don't confirm now, your subsidy could lapse and you'll have to reapply from scratch next month.

choices.text: Ask to see his BESCOM ID and a written notice or complaint number, note his name and phone number, then call BESCOM's official helpline (1912) or check the BESCOM app/website before sharing your Aadhaar, meter details, or any OTP.
choices.feedback: Correct. Genuine subsidy verification never needs an OTP — that code exists only to authorize bank or UPI transactions, not to 'confirm' you in a government scheme. Verifying independently through BESCOM's own helpline tells you whether he's real without handing over anything sensitive in the meantime.

choices.text: Read out the OTP that lands on your phone, since he already knew your meter number and about the scheme, so he must genuinely be from BESCOM.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Once a real verification drive is in the news, scammers doing the rounds often already have publicly available details like your meter number — that proves nothing about who's actually at your door. Reading out an OTP hands over control of your bank account or SIM, not your electricity subsidy.

choices.text: Let him in and hand over a photocopy of your Aadhaar card since he's asking politely and says it's just for the scheme records, but keep the OTP to yourself.
choices.feedback: Not sharing the OTP is right, but handing an Aadhaar photocopy to an unverified visitor is still risky — a paper copy can be reused elsewhere for identity fraud. Ask for ID and a callback number, and only hand over documents once you've verified him through BESCOM's own channel.

choices.text: Refuse to open the door or engage at all, and don't follow up, assuming any 'verification' knock during a news-covered drive must be a scam.
choices.feedback: Caution is good, but disengaging entirely risks missing your actual Gruha Jyothi verification and losing the subsidy if he was genuine staff. Ask for ID through the door or window, note his details, and call BESCOM's helpline yourself — verify before deciding, rather than defaulting to either extreme.

takeaways: No government scheme — Gruha Jyothi included — ever needs an OTP at your doorstep; an OTP only authorizes bank or UPI transactions, never a subsidy 'confirmation'.
Always ask for photo ID and note a doorstep visitor's name and phone number before sharing any document, and verify independently by calling BESCOM's helpline (1912) or checking its official app.
Don't hand over an Aadhaar photocopy to anyone unverified at your door — verifying through the official portal or app is safer than a paper copy that can be reused elsewhere.
